newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourses may extend cooperation agreement.
newsitem.headline: German bourses may extend cooperation agreement.

text.p: Cooperation agreements between Germany's stock exchanges may be extended to include all eight regional bourses instead of four at present, the Frankfurt stock exchange (FWB) said on Wednesday.

An FWB spokesman told Reuters the Frankfurt bourse was in favour of the Stuttgart, Bremen, Hanover and Hamburg exchanges joining an existing cooperation agreement between bourses in Frankfurt, Berlin, Duesseldorf and Munich.

The spokesman would neither confirm nor deny a report in German newspaper Boersen-Zeitung that a proposal to extend the agreement would be discussed at a meeting of the presidents of the various bourses this evening.
Two years ago the German regional bourses agreed a comprehensive cooperation proposal for the first time, but differences of opinion meant the proposal was never approved.
Germany's smaller stock exchanges fear a loss of influence and autonomy if they join up with larger counterparts, particularly the Frankfurt bourse, which dwarfs the rest.

Wolfgang Peterhoff, managing director of the Duesseldorf exchange, said a possible broadening of the co-operation would be on the agenda for the meeting, but could not say whether or not there would be a concrete proposal.
The meeting is due to take place after talks between the German stock exchange holding company Deutsche Boerse AG, the advisory board of the FWB and the advisory board of the German Futures Exchange.

Boersen-Zeitung said Deutsche Boerse was planning to centralise all German stock exchange data in one site and to set up a separate company to that end, but that a firm decision had yet to be reached.
